scope: Proposition 8.3 (The first attachment and its coefficient) of the manuscript “The metric Blaschke theorem” (preprints/The-metric-Blaschke-theorem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 344 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c631e2d36940a81e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an oriented rank-three vector bundle E → B and an attaching map f : S(E) −→ M. Let p : S(E) → B and put x = f∗u ∈ H4(S(E); Z). The following properties hold: (i) The pullback ρ∗E is the first negative bundle for the free-loop energy. It is isomorphic as a real vector bundle to the rank-three bundle K → U with fiber Kw = {a ∈ w⊥ : Ja(D) = 0}, Ja(0) = 0, J′ a(0) = a, where Ja is the normal Jacobi field along γw. (ii) Let e p : S(ρ∗E) → U and b ρ : S(ρ∗E) → S(E) be the pullback square. Then b ρ∗ x = e p∗ z. (8.10) (iii) After choosing the orientation of E, one has p!x = e. (8.11) With either orientation its coefficient is ±1. (iv) The actual negative bundle satisfies ρ∗ p1(E) = 4z. (8.12)
